# Production report — "What Happens When a Submarine Implodes?"

**Deliverable:** `sub/out/submarine_implosion_short.mp4` — H.264 High, 1080x1920, 30 fps, 37.0 s (1110 frames), AAC 48 kHz stereo, about -16 LUFS. ffprobe validation: `sub/out/ffprobe_validation.json`.
**Pipeline:** Blender 5.3 (Cycles, CPU only) with all geometry, materials and animation generated by Python -> Pillow/numpy compositor -> procedural sound design + Kokoro TTS (`am_adam`) -> FFmpeg.
**Files:** `sub/scripts/` (scene.py, tl.py, composite.py, audio.py, tts.py, assemble.py), `sub/blend/main.blend`, `sub/audio/vo/narration.wav`, `sub/audio/subtitles.srt`.

## What was built
- One original deep-sea submersible modelled procedurally (no downloaded assets): pressure hull with stiffener ribs, flanges and 112 bolts, acrylic viewport dome with a lit cabin behind it, external tube cage (3 hoops, rails, braces, skids), foam flotation block, battery pods, 4 thrusters with propellers, 4 spotlights with lenses, strobe antenna. Hull shader: panel seams, grime/streaks, bump, roughness variation.
- One underwater environment: deep blue-black volume with scattering, suspended particles, light beams, controlled dim fill.
- The implosion is a per-frame numpy deformation field (local dent -> propagating inward flattening and crumple, cage and fixtures follow, parts tumble off), plus debris cloud, hull shards, a faint pressure-wave shell. No fireball, no outward explosion.
- Cross-section: layered hull-wall ring (liner / composite / outer coat) buckling in a lobed mode with a stress colour map, external (blue) and internal (orange) pressure arrows.

## Honest limitations / deviations
- **Hook length:** the two required narration sentences take about 8 s at a calm pace, so the hook runs 0–8.3 s (not 0–5 s). Shot 1 is the extreme close-up (0–4.4 s), shot 2 the buckle + freeze + pull-back (4.4–8.3 s).
- **Model quality:** original procedural model; it reads as a credible research submersible but is simpler than a studio asset (no manipulator arm, no cabling, tube cage is smooth). Close-up surface detail is limited by 720x1280 render resolution (upscaled to 1080x1920).
- **Implosion timing:** the real event takes milliseconds; at 30 fps it is shown as ~2-3 frames ("FULL SPEED"), then a labelled 10x slow-motion replay. The collapse shape (flattening + crumple) is an illustrative visualization, not a finite-element simulation; real failure modes depend on hull design, material and damage.
- **Pressure-wave shell** and particle cloud are stylised; arrows and cross-section are labelled "illustrative, not to scale".
- **Audio** is synthesised and level-measured, not auditioned by ear. Music is sparse and drops out around the implosion.
- Rendering used CPU Cycles with a per-frame time cap, so some noise/denoise softness remains.
- Git push to GitHub fails with 403 (Claude GitHub App not installed on the repo); work is committed locally.

## Physics check
Gauge pressure at 3,800 m ~ rho*g*h = 1025 x 9.81 x 3800 ~ 38 MPa ~ 377 atm (about 378 atm absolute) -> "roughly 380 atmospheres", stated as "can exceed 380 times the pressure at the surface" per the brief ("nearly four kilometers"). Implosion described as an inward structural collapse driven by external pressure; failure mode not claimed to be universal; nothing is said about human bodies.
Note: main.blend holds geometry/materials/lights; the per-frame animation is applied by scene.py (frame handler), so render via the scripts.
